subject: Exec workshop — travel contingency & health advisory
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 15:03:00 -0000
Subject: Draft: travel contingency & on-site health guidance for Acme exec workshop

Team — putting this draft here so we can align before I loop in Acme and the hotel. Key objectives: keep the exec workshop on track while minimizing exposure risk, and have clear go/no-go thresholds and on-site responses. Highlights: 

- Pre-travel: require attendees to register travel plans with GlobalTravelPro, confirm travel insurance (business-plus), and share any recent medical advisories.
- Day-of: on-site point of contact (POC) from Redwood + Acme; designated quiet room for anyone who feels unwell.
- Incidents: documented escalation path (on-site med triage -> nearest clinic -> hospital transport); vendor (hotel) to confirm 24/7 emergency support.
- Cancel/remote triggers: local public health advisory level >= 3 OR airline cancellations affecting >25% of confirmed attendees within 72h — then shift to remote-first with a 48h notice where possible.

Please read the attached checklist and send edits by Monday EOD. I will compile and send to Acme and the Hilton after we converge.

Attachments: Travel_Safety_Checklist_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Draft: travel contingency & on-site health guidance for Acme exec workshop

Thanks Vanessa — a couple of suggested tweaks: 

- Add a line about reimbursement for last-minute hotel isolations and whether Redwood will cover that for our own attendees.
- Clarify timeline for the 48h remote shift notice (is it 48h before the start of the workshop or before the first affected attendee travel?).

Also, we should get Acme to confirm their emergency POC and whether they want name badges indicating emergency contact info (helps with contact tracing).

On the triggers, I agree with the >25% airline cancellations metric; maybe add a secondary trigger for local transit strikes.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hilton Downtown — EventOps <events@hiltondt.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 18:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Exec workshop — travel contingency & health advisory

Vanessa / team — thanks for the draft. A few notes from Acme's side: 

- We will confirm our internal POC (likely me and our Head of Compliance, Jason Wu) by Friday.
- The city health dept recently issued an advisory about a seasonal respiratory spike; they are at advisory level 2 now and trending up. Our travel policy team prefers a 72h notice for changes, but for execs we can make exceptions with approvals.
- Regarding reimbursements: Acme will cover vendor charges for meeting room cancellations; attendees' travel reimbursements should follow standard Acme travel policy.

Hilton Events has flagged that they can provide a quiet isolation room and local clinic contacts, but we need to provide headcounts and a schedule 7 days prior. I asked them to share clinic names and hours (cc'ed).

Best,
Sarah Chen
Director, Strategic Programs
Acme Financial
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Hilton Downtown — EventOps <events@hiltondt.com>, GlobalTravelPro <ops@globaltravelpro.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 14:07:00 -0000
Subject: Consolidated plan & final ask — Acme exec workshop (next week)

Team / Sarah — thanks for the quick turn. I consolidated the feedback and attached the final plan and a CSV of local clinic contacts pulled from Hilton and GlobalTravelPro. Key updates: 

- Notice window: we will operate on a 48h operational window for Redwood/Acme decision-making, but we will be prepared for exceptions at leadership discretion. Addendum in the doc clarifies approvals (VP+).
- Reimbursement approach: Redwood will cover isolated hotel stays for Redwood staff up to 3 nights when isolation is required by hotel/health authority; we will charge back otherwise per company policy.
- On-site ops: Hilton confirmed isolation room, daily cleaning increases for common areas, and on-call security (contact: events@hiltondt.com).
- Communication: Redwood will send an in-event SMS check-in to all attendees and a short daily health reminder.

Next steps: Sarah to confirm Acme POC and final headcount by Friday 26th; Hilton to confirm clinic hours by EOD Thursday 25th. If we don't get headcount by 26th 23:59, we proceed with current headcount and assume no extra rooms will be available.

Attachments: Travel_Safety_Checklist_v2.pdf (updated), Local_Clinic_Contacts.csv

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Consolidated plan & final ask — Acme exec workshop (next week)

Acknowledged. I have uploaded the checklist and emergency contact CSV to the shared Drive folder (link in plan). I will also brief our on-call CS lead on the communication templates for the SMS reminders.

One quick operational note: I'll confirm with Finance that the emergency hotel cover process is pre-approved for Redwood staff to avoid delays.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen

Redwood Inference
